definitions.explanation: Not showy or flashy. Describes something subdued in appearance or style.
Understated, without ostentation. Often used for colors, clothing, or personalities.

notes:
{地味|じみ} describes something plain, understated, or lacking in flashiness. It applies to appearance, personality, lifestyle, and work — anything that is quiet and unassuming rather than eye-catching.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {地味|じみ}に (plainly, modestly)
- Noun modifier: {地味|じみ}な + noun

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {地味|じみ}な⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧/⟦{色|いろ}→色：00849_iro⟧: plain clothes/colors
- {地味|じみ}な⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧: unglamorous work
- {地味|じみ}な⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧: quiet/reserved personality
- {地味|じみ}に⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧: to look plain

SLANG USAGE:
In casual modern speech, {地味|じみ}に can mean "low-key" or "surprisingly" — e.g., {地味|じみ}に⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧ (low-key delicious), {地味|じみ}に⟦{辛|つら}い→辛い：01112_tsurai⟧ (surprisingly tough).

SIMILAR WORDS:
{地味|じみ} vs ⟦{派手|はで}→派手：03563_hade⟧ (showy, flashy) is one of the most common antonym pairs in Japanese, used for clothing, personality, lifestyle, and events.
